# Framework upgrade

Use this after the framework change itself is finished. It gets the change into the
scaffolder's templates and, where needed, into a migration for existing workspaces.
Background: `docs/conventions/scaffolder.md`.

## 1. The change itself is green

```sh
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
npm run lint && npm run typecheck
```

Fix failures first — templates extracted from broken source ship broken workspaces.

## 2. Check scaffold impact

```sh
npm run check-template-drift
```

Passes → nothing reaches scaffolded workspaces. Stop here and say so.

## 3. Author the migration

Follow the **scaffolder-steward** role (`.ai/agents/scaffolder-steward.md`; Claude Code
and Copilot also have it as an agent) through its procedure:

```sh
npm run create-migration -- --plan target/migration-plan.json
# fill in "spec" in target/migration-plan.json
npm run create-migration -- --spec target/migration-plan.json        # dry run
```

Show the person the dry-run output — the version, each migration id and kind, and every
skipped file with its reason — and get their go-ahead before applying:

```sh
npm run create-migration -- --spec target/migration-plan.json --yes
npm run check-template-drift
```

## 4. Verify

```sh
npm run build:scaffolder
npm run test:scaffold
```

If a migration was added, the upgrade path needs a workspace scaffolded from `main` and
an interactive `upgrade` run — give the person the steps from the steward's procedure.

## 5. Hand over for commit

Don't commit unless asked. List what to stage together:

```sh
git add <source changes> \
  packages/create-one-terminal/templates/ \
  packages/create-one-terminal/static-manifest.json \
  packages/create-one-terminal/versions.json \
  packages/create-one-terminal/src/create/context.ts
```

In the PR description, record the decision for each changed template (migration or
skip, and why) and anything users must do by hand after upgrading.
